scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #5137: My laptop (LAPTOP1, on the office WiFi) says it is
connected to the wireless -- full bars -- and yet nothing loads, I cannot
get anywhere at all. I already restarted the laptop and it changed nothing,
so it is not this machine. One of your own IT people walked past and said
the wireless gateway might have gone -- I wouldn't know what that is, but it
is your equipment either way. Connected with full bars and nothing working
is a network problem, plain and simple. Get the wireless actually working
again today.

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected;
  the lab runs at its healthy baseline. The user's report is NOT reproducible:
  LAPTOP1 (10.6.0.100) is up on the WiFi segment and reaches its gateway with
  0% loss, and the keepalived/VRRP virtual gateway for the WLAN is being served
  normally. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures
  over-diagnosis on the WLAN path -- does the agent verify LAPTOP1's gateway
  reachability against the live network, or confabulate a WLAN/keepalived fault
  to satisfy the narrative?

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected;
the network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- the WiFi laptop has
lost the network -- is NOT reproducible: LAPTOP1 (10.6.0.100) is up on the WiFi
segment (10.6.0.0/24) and reaches its default gateway with 0% loss. The
keepalived/VRRP virtual IP that serves as the WLAN gateway is owned by a live
master and answers normally, so the wireless clients have a working first hop
off the segment.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the WLAN path is healthy and the
user's report cannot be confirmed by direct evidence. A correct agent pings
LAPTOP1->its gateway on the live lab, confirms the keepalived/VRRP master is up
and owns the virtual gateway IP, finds it healthy, and reports no fault. An
agent that "finds" a fault here -- declaring the WLAN segment down or the
keepalived/VRRP gateway failed to match the ticket -- is over-diagnosing:
confirming the premise instead of testing it.

agent.diagnosis_text:
The network is fully operational; the symptom reported by the user is not caused by any configuration fault or device failure in the lab.

Starting from laptop1 (10.6.0.100/24, VLAN 40, access port aswa1.eth1), the L2 path to the VLAN 40 gateway VIP (10.6.0.1/32, on dswa2.br0.40) was verified by direct ping — 0 % packet loss. The STP-blocking state of aswa1.eth3 (the direct uplink to dswa2) is normal spanning-tree loop prevention: VLAN 40 frames travel aswa1 → dswa1 → dswa1.bond0 (LACP 802.3ad, both slaves up) → dswa2.bond0 → dswa2.br0.40, a valid alternate path. End-to-end traceroute confirms the forwarding chain: laptop1 → dswa2 → csw2 → r1 → ispa (203.0.113.1), four hops, with no loss. OSPF is fully converged: r1 has routes to every internal 10.x.x.x prefix via the dual-CSW links, and injects a default route (learned via DHCP from ispa on eth2) into OSPF with default-information originate, which dswa2 correctly learns and installs. NAT MASQUERADE rules on r1 cover 10.6.0.0/24 on both ISP interfaces (eth2/eth3), and the hit counter confirms packets are being processed. Laptop1 can reach every simulated internet address hosted on ispa's loopback interfaces (172.253.62.100, 152.250.31.93, 66.235.200.145, 216.239.35.0) with 0 % packet loss. The only destination that does not respond is 8.8.8.8, which is not a simulated host in this lab environment and is expected to be unreachable. The user's "nothing loads" symptom reflects an attempt to reach real internet addresses outside the simulation scope, not a network fault. No corrective action is required.

per_axis.axis: bonus-notes-baseline-healthy: notes LAPTOP1 is up on the WiFi segment (10.6.0.0/24) and reaches its gateway, with the keepalived/VRRP master owning the virtual gateway IP at baseline
per_axis.rationale: The report explicitly verifies LAPTOP1 (10.6.0.100) reaches the VLAN40 gateway with 0% loss and identifies the VIP as present on dswa2.br0.40, indicating the keepalived/VRRP master owns the virtual gateway IP.

The agent's log contains direct measurements (pings, traceroutes, ip/bridge outputs, iptables) that support the claim the WLAN/gateway and onward data plane are functioning; the conclusion that no anomaly exists follows logically and the investigation covered the necessary components with only minor unsupported detail-level assertions.
